subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Henderson <thenderson@finovatebank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can keep momentum: 

What I heard:
- Use case: loan origination assistant + report generation for underwriting teams (pilot: 5000 monthly queries)
- Success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 350ms, cost target <$0.0008/token equivalent, and no PII persisted outside of their VPC
- Key technical concerns: model validation, data residency, and audit logs

Stakeholder map (ask):
- Economic buyer: please confirm who owns the budget for the pilot (CFO/VP Finance)
- Security/legal: we expect a brief security questionnaire and SOC2 artifact request
- Procurement: will need standard MSA + SOW and typical PO process
- Decision criteria: latency, cost per token, auditability, and ability to run in private deployment

Can you please: 
1) Fill out the attached Decision_Roles_Template.xlsx with names/titles and who will sign off on budget/legal/procurement?
2) Share the expected procurement timeline (days to PO) and any required procurement docs we should prepare (vendor questionnaire links, specific CLA/DPAs)
3) Confirm whether we should loop in your Head of Legal now or later in the process

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I’ll draft a short internal champion enablement packet (talk tracks + ROI slide) and a proposed SOW for your procurement team to review.
- Rishi (cc’d) can run a 30-min technical deep dive/demo for your engineering/security team next week.

If you can get the stakeholder template back by Friday that would be great — helps us prep the champion enablement materials and SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Decision_Roles_Template.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)

Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — FinovateBank

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers and initial mapping below. I filled the template and attaching it here (see inline).

Preliminary stakeholder list (internal):
- Andrew McCoy, CFO — economic buyer (final sign-off on budget)
- Sara Liu, Head of Legal — primary for contract review and DPA
- James Park, Head of Data & Analytics — technical champion (owns integration)
- Procurement team (procurement@finovatebank.com) — handles PO and vendor onboarding

Procurement timeline: usually 2–3 weeks from SOW to PO for pilot-sized deals, but that can stretch to 4–6 weeks if legal needs extra time. Procurement will reach out to review your SOW and vendor paperwork; they typically require: vendor W9, MSA, DPA, and our standard security questionnaire.

Security asks: Sara will want SOC2 Type II + pen test summary and a short description of how you handle KV cache and tokenization to avoid PII persistence. Can you provide SOC2 and a short security summary?

We should loop Sara now so she has visibility — I’ve cc’d procurement here. I’m available for the technical session next Thursday or Friday afternoon.

Thanks,
Tom Henderson
Director of Product 
FinovateBank
thenderson@finovatebank.com

Rishi — can you run the technical deep dive next week? Tom suggested Thursday or Friday afternoon; if those don’t work we can propose Tue/Wed. The session will cover: deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), quantization/perf tradeoffs, and security controls (KV cache, KMS integration, audit logs).

Tom — two quick asks for the champion enablement packet:
- Could you confirm the typical ROI metric Andrew cares about (cost savings vs. current inference ops, time-to-insight improvements, or risk reduction)?
- Any internal comms constraints (e.g., legal wording around vendor references)?

Thanks — I’ll also add the HubSpot deal link to the SOW for procurement reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FB-2027-034
